name: tmux-sessions
description: A sidebar for your tmux sessions: see which are busy, open one as a terminal, create, rename and kill. Sessions keep running when VS Code closes.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Sessions start in your home folder when the workspace is not a local folder.

viewsWelcome.contents:
tmux was not found on this machine.
Install it (macOS: brew install tmux, Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install tmux), or set its path in the tmuxSessions.tmuxPath setting.
[Refresh](command:tmuxSessions.refresh)

No tmux sessions yet.
[New session here](command:tmuxSessions.new)
A session keeps running after you close its terminal tab or VS Code.

tmuxSessions.socketName.markdownDescription: Which tmux server to use. A name (letters, numbers, dashes) selects a private server, the same as `tmux -L <name>`, so these sessions stay separate from any tmux you already use. Leave empty to use your default tmux server. Read from your user settings only.

tmuxSessions.newSessionCommands.markdownDescription: What **New Session Here** offers. `command` is typed into the new session and run; leave it empty for a plain shell. Read from your user settings only, so a folder you open cannot change what gets run.

enumDescriptions: In the order the sessions were created. The list never reshuffles.
By name, with numbers in order (api-9 before api-10).
tmuxSessions.sortBy.description: The order of the session list. Also switchable from the ... menu of the list.

tmuxSessions.hideStatusLine.description: Hide tmux's green status line in sessions created here (the terminal tab already shows the name). Applies to new sessions only.

tmuxSessions.refreshSeconds.description: How often the list refreshes while it is visible.

tmuxSessions.tmuxPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path of the tmux program, if it is not in a usual place. Read from your user settings only.
